name: Chablis Grand Cru
rightsHistoryPurpose: Official filiation, dated legal-entity rights and original-reference evidence for Chablis Grand Cru (#461). None establishes current farming.

namedPlots.coverageNote: BIVB lists seven climats, already mapped as INAO denominations 440–446. Seven reviewed cadastral name correspondences are audited without publishing a second layer. These are partial cadastral correspondences, not replacement climat boundaries. Four additional cadastral names remain unresolved. La Moutonne is not an eighth climat; its existing producer illustration is separate.

unresolved.name: Valmur / Les Clos
unresolved.reason: Two same-name cadastral features hold 29 mapped parcels. Within the Grand Cru, their union intersects official Valmur by 56,720.636 m² and Les Clos by 22,655.233 m². No single climat name is assigned to this cadastral name; retain its printed name and the official whole-cru fallback.

unresolved.name: Vaudésir / Grenouilles
unresolved.reason: This cadastral feature holds 40 mapped parcels and intersects official Vaudésir by 52,700.950 m² and Grenouilles by 263.739 m². It is not a separate official climat. Keep the cadastral name without a climat alias; the seven official outlines remain available.

unresolved.name: Les Preuses
unresolved.reason: Four mapped parcels use this cadastral name, contributing 8,815.472 m² inside the official Les Preuses outline. BIVB does not list it as a climat; spatial inclusion alone is not an exact-name alias.

unresolved.name: Les Clos
unresolved.reason: One mapped parcel uses this cadastral name. The feature intersects the Grand Cru by 242.904 m², principally in official Les Clos. BIVB does not list it as a climat; no alias is inferred.

unresolved.name: La Moutonne
unresolved.reason: Absent from the seven BIVB climats and from the pinned cadastral lieux-dits. The existing separately labelled producer illustration spans parts of Vaudésir and Les Preuses; it is not a cadastral boundary or an eighth climat. No parcel or holder assignment is made.
